headline: Brazil Central Bank Maintains Selic Rate at 13.75% Amid Fiscal Concerns
summary: The Brazilian Central Bank (Copom) maintained the Selic interest rate at 13.75%. Analysts suggest that without fiscal adjustments, high interest rates may continue to constrain economic growth through 2027.
why: The Selic rate is the primary tool for controlling inflation in Brazil; its level directly impacts borrowing costs, corporate investment, and consumer spending.
why_moved: The decision to hold rates steady, despite a slightly more flexible tone, signals ongoing caution regarding inflation and fiscal policy, impacting market expectations for future growth.
